title: Canada Invites 6,000 French-Speaking Candidates at CRS Cut-Off of 401
excerpt: The November 25 Express Entry draw was the 13th French-language round of 2026, taking the category to 66,500 invitations this year, with a profile cut-off of September 12.
body:
• Canada issued 6,000 invitations to apply for permanent residence on November 25 in a French-language proficiency Express Entry draw, with a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System score of 401.
  • To be considered, candidates needed a profile created before 9:59:55 p.m. UTC on September 12, 2026, and French-language ability is the category's entry condition — at least NCLC 7 in each of the four abilities, according to draw reporting.
  • The cut-off fell six points from 407 in the previous French-language draw on October 27, which issued 5,000 invitations; this was the 13th French-language draw of 2026, taking the category to 66,500 invitations this year.
  • If you received an invitation in this draw, you have 60 days to submit a complete permanent residence application — check your IRCC account for your exact deadline and the programme you were invited under.

Canada has invited 6,000 French-speaking candidates to apply for permanent residence in its November 25 Express Entry draw, CIC News reported. The draw required a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 401 and a candidate profile created before 9:59:55 p.m. UTC on September 12, 2026.

Who was invited — and who was not

This was a category-based draw for French-language proficiency only. Candidates without qualifying French-language ability were not in this round, however high their CRS score. Draw reporting notes that qualifying for the French-language category requires approved French test results showing at least NCLC 7 in each of the four language abilities, and eligibility under one of the federal programs managed through Express Entry. It was Canada's second Express Entry selection round under the revised CRS, and its 67th selection round of 2026, CIC News said.

The round was also the first French-language draw since November 3, when Canada introduced new CRS points for Canadian work experience or a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation, under a Labour Market Integration Factor. Moving2Canada's analysis said the new points did not appear to have moved this draw's cut-off.

How this draw compares

The previous French-language draw, on October 27, issued 5,000 invitations at a cut-off of 407. The November 25 cut-off of 401 sits within the 382 to 435 range seen for French draws this year, Moving2Canada said. French-language draws have issued 66,500 invitations across 13 rounds in 2026 — 42.2% of all Express Entry invitations this year, ahead of the Canadian Experience Class total of 57,750, according to the same analysis. In total, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada has issued 157,408 invitations in 2026, CIC News reported.

The November 3 points change behind this draw

As of November 3, 2026, Express Entry candidates can earn additional CRS points for Canadian work experience or a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation, under the new Labour Market Integration Factor that awards the higher of the two scores, CIC News reported. IRCC classifies 186 occupations as high-wage by occupation code, in three levels according to whether the occupation's national median wage is at least 1.3, 1.5, or two times the average median wage of the Canadian workforce. A qualifying job offer no longer requires a Labour Market Impact Assessment, and a temporary public policy in force from November 3 allows officers to exempt eligible invited candidates from that requirement for qualifying offers used for Federal Skilled Worker or Federal Skilled Trades eligibility, CIC News said.

What invited candidates do next

An invitation is not permanent residence. Candidates invited in this draw have 60 days to submit a complete permanent residence application, and should check their IRCC account for the exact deadline and the programme they were invited under, Moving2Canada said. Applicants already in Canada whose work permits are expiring may be eligible for a Bridging Open Work Permit while they wait, CIC News noted.

For candidates not invited, the draw offers a benchmark rather than a promise: French-language cut-offs have stayed in the low 400s through 2026, and Canada is targeting 31,825 French-speaking permanent resident admissions outside Quebec in 2027, rising to 12% of admissions outside Quebec by 2029, according to Moving2Canada. Improving an approved French test result toward or beyond NCLC 7 in every ability remains the direct route into this category.
